| | Folks: An update from the federal 8th Circuit on**one of the most dangerous anti-voter rulings we’ve seen in years**. A federal appeals court recently cut off a key avenue for private groups and individuals to bring racial discrimination claims under the Voting Rights Act (VRA). The ruling, which applies in seven states, further weakens the ability of our civil rights law to protect voters, and could lead to the Supreme Court settling the issue. This goes back to an initial ruling from 2023, the impact of which is pretty simple to understand: That voters and voting rights organizations can no longer sue to overturn unjust laws under the Voting Rights Act. According to the 8th Circuit, and now confirmed on appeal, only the Department of Justice (DoJ) has the legal standing to sue states over voting laws. clean_body: Democracy Docket: New Ruling Cuts Off Key Tool to Protect Minority Voters| | | Voters desperately need a "private right to action " to protect their rights. All that phrase means is that we, the people, can bring forward a lawsuit ourselves when we see wrongdoing in our elections. These 8th Circuit decisions strip us of that \-- in a world where most legal action around voting rights comes from groups like ours and our partners, not from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ). And we've got at least these four years of DOJ's Civil Rights division facing internal attacks from a hostile presidential administration that doesn't just believe conspiracy theories, but spreads them. = | = | | Folks: An update from the federal 8th Circuit onone of the most dangerous anti-voter rulings we’ve seen in years. A federal appeals court recently cut off a key avenue for private groups and individuals to bring racial discrimination claims under the Voting Rights Act (VRA). The ruling, which applies in seven states, further weakens the ability of our civil rights law to protect voters, and could lead to the Supreme Court settling the issue. This goes back to an initial ruling from 2023, the impact of which is pretty simple to understand: That voters and voting rights organizations can no longer sue to overturn unjust laws under the Voting Rights Act. According to the 8th Circuit, and now confirmed on appeal, only the Department of Justice (DoJ) has the legal standing to sue states over voting laws. With former Florida AG Pam Bondi -- a "big lie" spreading MAGA acolyte -- serving as Attorney General, it's clear that the DOJ is not going to protect voting rights over the next four years. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = | = | | = | = | = | | This is all about the legal term "private right of action". The 8th Circuit says it doesn't exist. That means the pro-voting lawsuits we've seen in states like Wisconsin, Georgia, Florida, and others nationwide wouldn't be possible anymore if the Supreme Court backs up this ruling. We won’t sugarcoat this: This could be a crushing blow to many voting rights organizations across the country, ourselves included. If this new appellate ruling is not overturned by the Supreme Court, it could unravel all of the great work pro-voting organizations are doing across the country — and allow dozens of unjust, unconstitutional voter restrictions to stand. Attacks like this on what remains of the Voting Rights Act are going to get worse over the next few years. As voter suppression laws become increasingly targeted and oppressive , our work to combat them must become smarter, stronger, and more accessible to everyone. = | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. You may not know this, but back in 2016, I made $24,000 a year as a legislator in the state Senate.
With two teenagers and rent to pay, my husband and I struggled to make ends meet. Like many Arizonans, I did what I had to do to provide for my family, and I made the decision to drive for Uber to help pay the bills.
It was hard to struggle financially, and I never wanted my kids to worry. But when you're a parent, you do whatever is necessary to put food on the table and keep the lights on.
I’ll never forget those late nights at the kitchen table, staring at a stack of bills. I know deeply what it’s like to do what you have to do for your family.
**As governor, I’ve always pledged to do the same for yours — and together, we’ve delivered on that promise.**
We passed the Arizona Promise Budget, which will help make childcare more affordable, provide 10 million free meals to working-class children, and increase funds for K-12 education.
Through executive action, we erased $429 million in medical debt for more than 352,000 Arizonans and helped Arizonans save up to 80% on life-saving prescriptions.
It’s a testament to what’s possible when we put people above politics and deliver common-sense solutions for families across our state.
But because of MAGA Republicans in Washington, over 365,000 Arizonans stand to lose their healthcare coverage. Countless families will suddenly lose their food assistance benefits.
**It’s a disgrace. It’s a slap in the face to working families. And Andy Biggs, one of my GOP opponents, didn’t just vote for it — _he said it doesn’t go far enough._ We can’t let him get anywhere close to the Governor’s Office.**
Peter, ultimately, I got into public service because our elected officials are supposed to fix the issues we’re facing, not exacerbate them.
Working families shouldn’t be forced into difficult financial decisions because an out-of-touch politician voted to give a tax break to billionaires. Arizonans deserve a leader who understands firsthand the value of every dollar and the dignity of hard work.
So as MAGA Republicans like Andy Biggs and Karrin Taylor Robson attack our progress, it’s only strengthening my commitment to deliver for the hardworking people of this state.
[If you agree we deserve leaders who deliver for everyone and not just the ultra-wealthy, please consider chipping in $10 to Yassamin and my campaign today. We’ve got a long fight ahead, and it’s going to take everyone to win this race and defend our values.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116209445/572822365/-1981658856?refcode=AU_YA_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20250929_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZWVlOTlmMC05MDlkLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=C8YqdU8AOcrR3QtQ_tnsY-luQTorY4VBZW_IjHvazX4=)

I wanted to reach out personally about someone I believe in deeply: Dr. Raul Ruiz, Congressman. Raul’s race in California’s 25th District is one of the most closely watched in the country — and if Republicans flip this seat, it’ll be a big step backward in our push to take back the House in 2026. The truth is, the stakes couldn’t be higher. Republicans aren’t even trying to govern anymore. They’ve abandoned any effort to hold Donald Trump accountable for his authoritarian impulses — and they’ve chosen chaos over country again and again. Now they’re pushing us closer to another government shutdown, and it's working families in California who will pay the price. That’s why we need Raul in Congress. Raul is a fighter. A doctor. A public servant who’s shown time and again that he puts people over politics. Whether it’s standing up to RFK Jr.’s dangerous vaccine conspiracies or pushing back against MAGA extremism in Congress, Raul has never backed down from a tough fight. But there’s no sugarcoating it: this race is going to be a dogfight. Trump gained 13 points in CA-25 between 2020 and 2024, and Republicans are laser-focused on flipping this district. Peter, I want to take a quick moment to fill you in on everywhere the NDRC and this movement are fighting to defeat Republican attempts to cheat in the midterm elections:
* Just like in **Texas** , the fair maps movement is challenging **Missouri’s** new gerrymandered map that’s designed to pick up an additional GOP seat that Republicans just forced through.

* Republicans are trying to pull off an even more extreme gerrymander in **Ohio**. We’re mobilizing on the ground to help empower Ohio voters who are adamantly against this partisan power grab.

* The White House is pursuing an intense pressure campaign to get **Indiana** lawmakers to force a redraw of their congressional map — even threatening “consequences” for the state’s funding if they don’t follow through. We’re doing everything we can to strengthen bipartisan opposition to stop this redistricting rampage from expanding any further.

* ...and much, much more.

This list says two things: One, we have to be ready for anything and everything the Republicans throw at us to grab power for themselves. And two — this is an enormous undertaking that requires unprecedented resources. [**How much we raise this month will determine whether we can ramp up our efforts in these states or whether we’ll have to make tough calls on where to pare back. clean_body: How much we raise this month will determine whether we can ramp up our efforts — or if we have to pare back. | Peter, I want to take a quick moment to fill you in on everywhere the NDRC and this movement are fighting to defeat Republican attempts to cheat in the midterm elections: Just like in Texas , the fair maps movement is challenging Missouri’s new gerrymandered map that’s designed to pick up an additional GOP seat that Republicans just forced through. Republicans are trying to pull off an even more extreme gerrymander in Ohio. We’re mobilizing on the ground to help empower Ohio voters who are adamantly against this partisan power grab. The White House is pursuing an intense pressure campaign to get Indiana lawmakers to force a redraw of their congressional map — even threatening “consequences” for the state’s funding if they don’t follow through. We’re doing everything we can to strengthen bipartisan opposition to stop this redistricting rampage from expanding any further. ...and much, much more. This list says two things: One, we have to be ready for anything and everything the Republicans throw at us to grab power for themselves. And two — this is an enormous undertaking that requires unprecedented resources. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = We’re not only playing defense in states like Missouri, Ohio, and Indiana. We’re working to elect pro-democracy champions to the Virginia Governor’s mansion and in the House of Delegates — building a pathway to constitutional changes to the redistricting commission. We’ve endorsed three Democracy Defenders in the Pennsylvania State Supreme Court fight. Peter,

_Will your children and grandchildren inherit a free country from you?_

_Have you done everything you can to ensure they thrive in an America as great as the one you grew up in?_

I think everyone wants to say they have, because _failing to do so is the kind of regret you’ll never outlive._

My name is Hayden Padgett. As a husband and father of two young children, I worry about the legacy I’m leaving behind for my kids, and I lose sleep at night knowing the future of America is in great danger.

That’s why I serve as chairman of the Young Republican National Federation – where we lead the fight for the next generation of Republicans – and why I’m asking YOU to partner with us today.

We saw Charlie Kirk set the example. Nobody will be able to fill his shoes.

But he proved that the only way to help young people think for themselves and counter the rising tide of socialism is to speak boldly, engage in the national debate, and organize young voters to help save our country.

I could ignore what’s going on in the world. I could leave it up to someone else to fight for America’s future and enjoy my weekends watching football.

But the future of my kids is too important.

And like you, I REFUSE to take a passive stance in this fight.

clean_body: | | | | Peter, Will your children and grandchildren inherit a free country from you? Have you done everything you can to ensure they thrive in an America as great as the one you grew up in? I think everyone wants to say they have, because failing to do so is the kind of regret you’ll never outlive. My name is Hayden Padgett. As a husband and father of two young children, I worry about the legacy I’m leaving behind for my kids, and I lose sleep at night knowing the future of America is in great danger. That’s why I serve as chairman of the Young Republican National Federation – where we lead the fight for the next generation of Republicans – and why I’m asking YOU to partner with us today. We saw Charlie Kirk set the example. Nobody will be able to fill his shoes. But he proved that the only way to help young people think for themselves and counter the rising tide of socialism is to speak boldly, engage in the national debate, and organize young voters to help save our country. I could ignore what’s going on in the world. I could leave it up to someone else to fight for America’s future and enjoy my weekends watching football. But the future of my kids is too important. And like you, I REFUSE to take a passive stance in this fight. Every Young Republican volunteer has made the conscious decision to sacrifice their time and resources in order to leave this country better than we found it. But the harsh reality is, without your generous support behind us, our mission will weaken, starve, and eventually die out. | | "Tax cuts for the rich" is a favorite argument of those who oppose lower tax rates. But does imposing higher tax rates on wealthy Americans actually increase the amount of revenue coming into the federal government? Hoover Institution Senior Fellow **Thomas Sowell takes an empirical approach** in his commentary, [**_"_****_Trickle Down " Theory and "Tax Cuts for the Rich._****_"_**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2oumeso1fj8a3q9demvkm642aepgu95kercroc0_rp22sh2s8i6epb4s9h66ob1cdh2bs) Sowell separates fact from fiction when it comes to tax rates and uses real life data and examples to prove that lower tax rates for all actually lead to greater revenue for the government. ## Trump, Netanyahu Unveil Gaza Plan
President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday [unveiled a joint plan to end the Gaza war](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupSAQBuCn0Q6DiHgsKLY53d12SzPCqGwGMIDHdZ9-w32F7SYzyZ_5_l9fyxc4cmH_CR512eIS8M6EpWBadvgLJ4LBkyCskHEFopPgWQQXI-MzG_hiwdGzyNbqDVHg0KLup3EWQqnXqz20MrJXYhvlCmrgUlijBg4jTLy3AHJuna5pfB54z7mUUze8tmlU_Ww2NDP02EiO1pWYut_RhXLgRk_8YOpM9C3po5QzN8OPRrwb8b7vu9vin6qo97qJiWwj3iVd_mRX-KCjzARnZ01j1cYymish-8ayymYuGLqsCzvbE4RShxw9sgM8ZObRr5gyAx8wl6dN2p63I3JZTY3kuwdH3--V_-r0o8W_AAAA___kgI6Y), dependent on Hamas agreeing to a ceasefire and releasing all hostages within 72 hours of Israel accepting the proposal. The 20-point framework would create a temporary “Board of Peace,” to be chaired by Trump and joined by former U.K. Prime Minister Tony Blair, to oversee Gaza’s governance and reconstruction, with Israeli withdrawal tied to Hamas disarmament. [Read the full plan here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTUB0NaiXqp2CRRp3TphTW4tLaYCUSJGPDOf2D3hVePcAMvvlzX-_IwufzNx7kaojrSe8iVCvl9Yn_MRFulATPBxZ6oEgS_KxgwGoz686sHlk-a994F4iAuoZcO9oZYBimqdmdn4DMNkze-Bl6sGGewjQOj7HbKFjrG3ZXm5k70xrT9-Otm8Joh3beAm0ztqR6Q55rzLe_kc-6U5BPfFG-bfFoxO21pqK6XwoWBUvdaWeRK1Ow7PGgC6RgQX_wyaVmrBxPBYu1MFrT60zo9UXVpWZOeiMsFDiTrvnfkTSXjCQKliY7n94swmUYVW-eB_L3UFN_9NzLwVcAAAD__zwbg0k). [Netanyahu also apologized](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAQhp8Gd6wwsItdUGwUubtrUkRKY43NYE_CggPcOr6nj7yvcOXok-b__-_n2_gGFCgu7_BAW30aI-4lYK2YxwU-YUOYcQsQJyg4QQhbgGOUQl656LkSowMKx6gbZz2iRNWgbc21l_J267pmtUZf-67zk3Ng9KRnKdA4IybwMEk1mYbs-U30SrRCaG0uqvPmemv72ePcQ4tMC3RUU778ThTrij4c6Yn5MqdHE-xa61aYujM5MDns-355lHgyJgeM_KMwOZyjTphycK-zQjxg_eCwpZAW-sTCa-J_oULmPmX-pBSgUlx4OaOQllgPvlNdOVAuNdMfZHKAzO_39v3f8qtjakgzOaa-fzt14l5-YN6abN22UwhUboZpsTyAwqt4_ZLtp5X_AwAA__8jM5dW) in a “heart-to-heart” call with Qatar’s leader for Israel’s recent strike on Hamas officials in Doha, which killed a Qatari serviceman and drew sharp regional backlash. The Palestinian government in the West Bank welcomed Trump’s proposal and pledged reforms, including elections and an end to militant stipends. Hamas negotiators are reviewing the deal, but their refusal to disarm remains the key obstacle.

Officials in Florida say a man was killed after [getting caught in a rip current](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1yqzAQxfGngc7M6gPJKlTcxp1vm5JZxMoosyACGivk6TNOHiHtmTO_4v92H-6YOK2P_7iQLzEPK9WDqRTahwd-4UYYaGNcRzxoROaN8RwkyP4C7qJgmDDxOeh28pFIkmrJC9s7KY25XtvZw6StHlWQwoyhjxCM0wIEOIdonbZt8i8NnAIBoLXt1DXa3ggXIgWHghoNNKWS9-49p7XMFPnMT9q7kJeW_VzKdjTqXyNvjbzVWruYPythmX8vrxFLmBt5i0u4bDOCyno_gvqQbEK7-2mriTkdxjYaHgsm_qHLn3o8vfwOAAD__0hmc4o) over the weekend. Friend, Even now... it still doesn't feel real that we lost Charlie. His voice, his courage, his conviction -- it shaped all of us. And his vision -- **to build the most faithful and the most patriotic generation in American history** -- is why Turning Point USA exists today. Friend, that's why we have an inspiring update for you... In just the first seven days since Charlie was taken from all of us, Turning Point USA has received more than 54,000 requests from students who want to start or join a chapter:
---

**God is so good.** ✝️🙏🕊️ To give you perspective, Friend... Coming into this school year, Turning Point USA had roughly 900+ college chapters and 1,200+ high school chapters. It took us years to build those chapters... over a decade in fact... _But now?_ These students who signed up? They weren't asked to... They weren't recruited... **They felt it was their time to stand up for this country and honor Charlie.** Because of the life he lived. The faith he had. The love he showed God, his family, and others. The courage he had to speak truth. And his vision of a better America for us all.

He always believed this day would come. He used to talk about it all the time -- how the momentum would shift, how young people would rise up with courage, and how a Turning Point USA chapter would be in every college and high school in America. And now... _It 's happening._ Faster than he could have imagined. Bigger than we thought possible. And more beautiful than we can even describe. **Again, Friend, God is so good.** Since we lost Charlie, we've also felt SO MUCH love... Prayers. Emails. Messages. Stories about how Charlie's voice changed lives... or your children's or grandchildren's lives. And so many supporters have asked, _" What can I do?"_ As you read this, our team is working around the clock to follow up with every chapter request. And we're going to need help equipping them with our activism kits. **Every new chapter receives these kits from Turning Point USA with everything they need to get started -- including: ** ✅ Leadership materials
✅ Pocket Constitutions
✅ Chapter training tools
✅ American flags & patriotic gear Friend, I'm sure you'd believe it when we say it... _this won 't be a small task. _ But we're going to do it. Whatever it takes. **_For Charlie._** _And here 's how YOU can help with this..._ **Every $25 you give today helps stock another activism kit -- ready to deploy into a new Turning Point USA student chapter...** How many of these activism kits can you help provide to the wave of new student chapters that are just getting started?

## New Strategy to Stop Screwworm
The Texas Department of Agriculture announced it will [install fly traps](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAUBOCnwZ2twwFfm4JiG3fZdksLzEmMxI8FKCRvv0pe4dYjfaOZf7f9Znzw6fHXRNLtdc97ol4DtUZlP8kmE6l2nxKVahJFKg9Kx46A8whqFLA748N7l4PTFpziA2m-zAoFcMGHU4Nb5lXeJTjJpbIohDrs6lYyP9a6mQavPxgoAZwDwjLhTDi7RVlHVihOTAI533KZ2kmNXqbewzs_qUxHjkPQZ2tXZeIPw43h1nufjrPk9EkZbp85DDdTmj8CMdzqUaj3XOL4tcZIL3_ksRVz1fEyxVTfaEQOC8p5na7zGop2V_ch-PqzMAmPaHz4lrffXfbU-D8AAP__eNCBkg) along the border with Mexico to "monitor, detect, and stop" the spread of the parasitic New World screwworm, which has been confirmed 70 miles from the border and poses a major threat to the state's cattle industry. If enough supporters chipped in $3 before midnight, we’d be on our way to hitting our end-of-quarter goal – and keep this important fight going strong. body:
| Peter, as the kids say: You up?

I know I am! There's nothing I love more than getting up bright and early, making breakfast, and heading out for a run before diving into teaching my classes and working on this campaign.

I hope I'm not catching you too early, but it's the end of the quarter, it's 7 AM, and I couldn't wait to check in with you.

End-of-quarter deadlines are different from our usual end-of-month goals. At the end of a normal month, we're focused on keeping this campaign running strong. But today's deadline is about much more than that. Every dollar raised in these last hours will be reported to the FEC, and those reports will be made public. That means everyone — including Mariannette Miller-Meeks — will see the strength of our campaign.

name: Mikie Sherrill
subject: The state of this race
body:
This email is long, but I hope you’ll read all of it.
With just 35 days to go until Election Day, I wanted to send you an update about where our campaign stands heading into the final weeks of this race. This email is long, but I hope you’ll read all of it.
**[And if you’re already ready to power my campaign to victory, I’d really appreciate it if you chipped in before the end-of-quarter deadline tonight->](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250930-1?refcode=em-20250930-1&refcode2=686_1086043_AlCrB7&akid=686%2E1086043%2EAlCrB7)**
**The Polls Are Tied** Anyone who believes this race is anything but a toss-up needs to wake up, Peter. A new major poll was just released showing me deadlocked with my opponent, and with New Jersey becoming more competitive every year, this race is going to be _close._ But 11% of voters are still undecided, and I’m making it my personal mission to reach every single one of them before Election Day.**
**Ballots Are Already Out** As of last week, the first votes have been cast in our race for governor. Last governor's election, 22% of voters sent in their ballots by mail — and if those numbers stay the same, that means that a decisive margin of voters are going to be making their final decision in this race _before Election Day._ **That’s why I’m going to spend the next 35 days trying to reach as many voters as I can, and share with them my vision for our state.**
**The Stakes Couldn’t Be Higher** There is so much on the line for the Garden State in this election, Peter — lowering the cost of living, improving education for our children, fixing our public transportation, and more. But the way I look at it, we aren’t just deciding New Jersey’s future this November. This is our chance to show **the entire nation** that the people reject the Trump administration’s incompetence and authoritarianism. They’ve shown time and time again that they’ll do anything to stop me — _and that’s why meeting our fundraising goals is so important._
**[Peter, if anything I said convinced you, we have the last end-of-quarter deadline of the campaign tonight. We’re in a fight for the future of New Jersey, and I’m relying on the strength of our grassroots team to help us meet our goal. Can I count on you to pitch in a donation split between my team and Wes Moore and help me win this toss-up race?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250930-1?refcode=em-20250930-1&refcode2=686_1086043_AlCrB7&akid=686%2E1086043%2EAlCrB7)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250930-1?amount=5&refcode=em-20250930-1&refcode2=686_1086043_AlCrB7&akid=686%2E1086043%2EAlCrB7)**
Thank you, Peter. Let’s get to work.
— Mikie Sherrill

**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-footer?refcode=em-20250930-1&t=1&refcode2=686_1086043_AlCrB7&akid=686%2E1086043%2EAlCrB7)**

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks. **She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.** Nancy is fighting to:

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency
* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free
* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate
* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think
* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry **[formally requested federal authorization to activate up to 1,000 National Guard](https://substack.com/redirect/28dad26e-a44e-4c53-902b-a56033d71b9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** personnel under Title 32 authority, submitting the request to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to address overwhelming public safety concerns.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28dad26e-a44e-4c53-902b-a56033d71b9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Crime crisis cited as justification** : Landry cited Louisiana's violent crime rates that are 44.8% higher than the national average, with cities like Shreveport, Baton Rouge, and New Orleans experiencing homicides, carjackings, and gang violence, while local police forces face critical manpower shortages compounded by hurricane response duties.
* **Guard 's intended role**: Under Title 32 authority, National Guard troops would patrol high-crime neighborhoods, bolster police presence in major cities, provide logistical and communication support, and secure critical infrastructure, with Landry pointing to a 50% crime reduction during previous Guard deployments at Mardi Gras.
* **Mixed local reception** : While Landry insists the crisis demands urgent action and cites Louisiana's ranking among the nation's most dangerous states (520 violent crimes per 100,000 people in 2024), some local officials in Shreveport and New Orleans have voiced concerns, leaving the final decision in Defense Secretary Hegseth's hands.

Sherrod Brown

In America, rights don't trickle down from politicians. They aren't favors handed out by a benevolent state. Our Founders said--loudly--that rights come from God and government's job is to secure them, not invent them. That's the heart of the American idea. And it's very different from how many other countries talk about rights today.
The Declaration of Independence couldn't be clearer: we are "endowed by our Creator with certain unalienable Rights," and governments are instituted to secure those rights. Translation: rights exist before government, above government, and against government when it overreaches. The Constitution was written with that assumption baked in. That's why the Bill of Rights reads like a set of chains on Washington--"Congress shall make no law..."--and why the Ninth Amendment reminds us that the people retain rights beyond the ones listed on parchment. James Madison and Alexander Hamilton argued about whether a bill of rights was even necessary, precisely because the federal government was supposed to be limited to the few powers we delegated to it. Limited government only makes sense if the citizen's rights are older and higher than any statute.
Now, how does that compare to the rest of the world?
Some nations come close in language. Ireland's constitution speaks of "inalienable... rights... antecedent and superior to all positive law." Canada's Charter nods to "the supremacy of God and the rule of law." Switzerland's preamble invokes God. Germany's Basic Law grounds the whole order in "inviolable and inalienable human rights" and binds the state to human dignity. You can hear the echo of natural rights in those documents. They still operationalize rights through courts and charters, but the premise--there is something higher than the state--is at least acknowledged.
Others take a secular natural-rights approach. France's 1789 Declaration calls liberty and property "natural and imprescriptible." Modern international documents like the Universal Declaration of Human Rights talk about "inherent dignity." That's not theology, but it's still a statement that rights aren't the playthings of politicians.
And then there's the parliamentary model, led by the United Kingdom. The UK has proud traditions of liberty, but the operating rule is parliamentary sovereignty: Parliament can make or unmake any law. Rights are what Parliament says they are this session, tempered by politics and, more recently, by human-rights statutes that Parliament can also revise. That's the opposite of our starting point. In America, the people are sovereign and we loan the federal government a few enumerated powers. In the UK model, the legislature is sovereign and rights live or die on its say-so.
Why does this matter? Because the philosophical starting line determines the finish line when things get hard. When you believe government grants rights, then every crisis becomes an excuse to "temporarily" adjust them. When you believe rights are God-given and pre-political, the burden flips: the state must justify every infringement against a higher standard. That's not just wordplay. It's the difference between "You can speak because we allow it" and "You can speak unless we can meet a strict constitutional test to stop you." It's the difference between "You can worship unless the minister of regulations says otherwise" and "Government must keep its hands off your conscience."
We're seeing the clash of these worldviews right now. Plenty of modern officials talk like rights are downstream of legislation or agency rulemaking. Sorry--that's not the American creed. The oath they take isn't to a stack of regulations. It's to a Constitution designed to fence the government in on all sides so your pre-existing rights have room to breathe.
This is where conservatives and libertarians should plant the flag. School boards, city councils, state agencies, Congress--it doesn't matter. When anyone acts like your rights are permissions, push back. Remind them that the right to speak, to worship, to defend yourself, to be secure in your home, to be free from warrantless searches, to educate your children--these are not gifts. They're yours by birth, not by bureaucrat.
America is not perfect. No nation is. But our founding premise is unmatched: rights first, government second. Many countries nod toward that idea; some reject it outright. We should not follow them down the path where lawmakers become the source of liberty. That road always ends the same way--rights shrink when the wrong people are in power. The American path insists on the opposite: your rights don't depend on who holds the gavel.
So let's recover some old wisdom. Teach the Declaration like it matters. Read the Ninth and Tenth Amendments like they're real. Elect men and women who understand that power is supposed to be hard to use. And the next time a politician suggests your rights come from government, answer with the confidence of a free citizen: No--they come from God. Government's job is to keep its hands off.

Two minutes, null.

All I need is just a couple minutes of your time to explain what's at stake in Michigan.
**We've set a $300,000 end-of-quarter goal – and this comes as polling shows me _statistically tied_ with my Republican opponent. That means if I'm going to pull ahead and win, I need to raise every dollar I can right now.**
**[So please, before my critical midnight deadline – before our fundraising numbers go public – will you rush a donation of $5 or more to defeat Mike Rogers and keep Michigan blue?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/6302?t=3&akid=954%2E49239%2Ev0b5NZ)**
| | [Donate Now](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/6301?t=4&akid=954%2E49239%2Ev0b5NZ)
---
This goal means everything, null. Last cycle, the GOP spent nearly **$80 million** to try and turn Michigan red – and this time around, they're gearing up to spend _even more._
I've spent my entire life fighting for Michigan families. But I cannot compete with that kind of money unless grassroots supporters like you step up at this critical moment.
**Hitting this deadline will ensure we have the resources to reach voters where they are and turn this Toss Up race into a seat that helps us win back the Senate.** **[So with my two minutes up, I have to ask: Will you make a donation now – of $5 or whatever you can spare today – to win this race and restore our Democratic Senate majority?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/6301?t=5&akid=954%2E49239%2Ev0b5NZ)**

Thank you,

Haley

**A note from Haley Stevens:** null, I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. That’s why I’ve fought so hard for working families my entire life. Now, I’m running for Michigan’s open Senate seat to continue fighting for the people and communities I love. The path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan, which means this race is shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive in the entire country. Haley

Peter,

The situation in Texas is becoming increasingly dire. Women in red states need our support.

**As of LAST WEEK: the majority-male Texas Legislature has passed a ‘bounty hunter’ bill that would allow _private_ _citizens_ to _sue_ ANYONE for providing abortion medication in Texas. And, Governor Greg Abbott has officially signed it into law. **

According to the _Amarillo Globe News_ , _"Abortion-inducing medication is already outlawed in Texas and for years, Texas has allowed private citizens to sue abortion providers. The bill does not introduce new bans to abortion and it applies an existing legal tool — private enforcement — to the abortion pill ban more specifically. But, it introduces to the abortion fight a novel 'bounty hunter' provision by giving a monetary award to those who bring a lawsuit and are not related to any part of the pregnancy."_

---
| | [ STAND WITH KEEPING OUR GOVERNMENT FUNDED ➜ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116232447/572932857/1060786640?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NDcyOWZiMy0wNzllLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FEmouefuuDlB7zoBCcEzuAid2_UHkQ-DBbKh6cMJ8_E=)

Republicans have majorities in the House, Senate AND we have a Republican president. They have the power to avert a shutdown, but instead, they're prioritizing preserving tax cuts for billionaires over our healthcare and funding our government. **As long as Republicans have majorities in Congress, this is the dysfunction we can expect. If we want the madness to stop, we need to win back Democratic majorities in the House and Senate next year.** **It's that simple. However, to do that, we need your support. Our goal of a Democratic Congress is achievable, but to get there, the work begins right now.** Will you stand with us as we work to take back power for the American people? disclaimer_text: Paid for by State Democrats Committee (StateDemocrats
body:
We don’t want to show any weakness.
#

**[Our campaign’s first FEC end-of-quarter filing deadline is just hours away. Split a donation of any size between our team and State Democrats Committee to help meet our goal before time runs out.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/96191?refcode=em20250930-9509&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9509%2E614464%2EBXxJQl)**
---
Hello Peter,
I’m reaching out about our upcoming filing deadline — the first of our campaign so far — but I wanted to make sure you had some important context:
**Nationwide, Republicans and GOP-aligned groups have been outraising Democrats in the lead-up to next year’s midterm elections, and our election in North Carolina is expected to become the most expensive U.S. Senate race in history.**
My GOP opponent and his allies will be forced to make spending decisions they may not want to make based on what we can raise now, Peter. With all that in mind, it’s even more important for us to show our financial strength in this report.
This is the most consequential Senate election of 2026, and if we win here, Democrats have the chance to take back the majority and stop the far-right’s extreme agenda. Meeting our fundraising goals is key to our chances of success in this toss-up race.
But we have a long way to go to hit our end-of-quarter target, and we’re running out of time to get there.
**[We can’t risk allowing my GOP opponent to outraise us, so I need your help right away. Does a contribution, split between our campaign and State Democrats Committee, fit in your budget today?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/96191?refcode=em20250930-9509&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=9509%2E614464%2EBXxJQl)**
**[DONATE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/96191?refcode=em20250930-9509&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=9509%2E614464%2EBXxJQl)**
Thank you,
Roy Cooper

subject: PA News Story: RITE Lawsuit over Mismatched Voter ID Information to be Argued Oct 7th
body:
RITE seeks to to restore common sense on Voters ID verification |
---
| |
---
| | **PA News Story: RITE Lawsuit over Mismatched Voter ID Information to be Argued Oct 7 th**
**PENNSYLVANIA** – Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect election security and integrity, today highlighted a news story previewing an important voter identification lawsuit in Pennsylvania to be argued on October 7. The Delaware Valley Journal [examined the issues in the case](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=10dc98a382&e=ea91f782ea) and spoke to RITE President Justin Riemer for the piece. And excerpt is below:
_For years, when registering to vote, Pennsylvanians could list driver’s license numbers or Social Security numbers that did not match government databases on their applications._

_The Department of State and Secretary Al Schmidt instructed county boards of elections to stand down and refrain from verifying voters’ identities in the event of a mismatch, according to a lawsuit that seeks to remedy this._
_**_
_RITE President Justin Riemer told DVJournal that while there’s been other litigation on the topic, “they did not use the same legal claims.”_

_“The issue that we’ve identified, which is a directive from the state in 2018, [is] that the counties cannot reject voter registration applications where the driver’s license or the last four digits of the Social Security number do not match what’s found in the official government databases,” said Riemer. “The counties used to verify registrations. That the counties cannot reject those mismatched applications, it’s something that other groups have tried to pursue, but they’ve used a different theory than our case.”_

_“Our case is based entirely on state law,” he said._
To read more, please visit the [Delaware Valley Journal](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=ebc88ff4cd&e=ea91f782ea). RITE is at the forefront of pursuing litigation and investigations to shore up weaknesses in states’ voter registration and mail voting systems. Our litigation in states like [Pennsylvania](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=7f3f527875&e=ea91f782ea) aims to fix porous processes that fail to verify the eligibility and identity of individuals before they are registered and can vote. RITE also actively litigates to ensure states are verifying the identity of those casting mail ballots.
###

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: This comes from the heart

body:
I hope you’ll take a moment to read this
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-sep25.vnrwKJ&refcode=em250930-1-b&t=1&akid=10918%2E3935704%2EjxAFvm)
---
Hello there,
It’s Gabby Giffords. This email is longer than the ones I usually write, but I hope you’ll take a moment to read it. It comes from the heart.
We are living in challenging times. This summer has been nonstop headlines about gun violence. From my friend, Minnesota House Speaker Melissa Hortman, to Charlie Kirk, to school shootings across the country, we have seen the toll of gun violence far too often.
These recent events hit home for me.
Nearly 15 years ago, I was the victim of gun violence. I was hosting a constituent event when a gunman opened fire, killing six people and wounding 13 others. Many news outlets declared I was dead. Doctors called it a miracle that I survived.
But the shooting left me partially paralyzed on my right side and impacted my ability to speak. I spent six months in a rehabilitation center, relearning how to walk and talk. My recovery still continues today.
One thing I’ve learned since my shooting is the importance of looking forward. I don’t spend any time thinking about the man who shot me. I am focused on the lives that we can save — the families who can be spared what mine has gone through.
So when I see another shooting happening on my TV screen, I feel angry. Angry that there is so much senseless gun violence that we can stop.
Gun violence isn’t a Democrat versus Republican issue. Everybody deserves to live their lives free from fear.
In my heart, I know that we can stop gun violence. But what this requires is our elected officials having the courage to stand up to the gun lobby as if our future depends on it. Because they do.
That is my mission, and our mission at GIFFORDS. We are working to invest in hard-to-reach communities and elect gun safety champions. **And thanks to supporters like you, gun safety is a winning issue.**
Now, we are entering the next phase of our fight, and we need more grassroots support. So here comes the part where I have to ask.
Tonight is our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline — our biggest deadline yet this year. After the clock strikes midnight, our team will see how much we’ve raised and decide where we have the resources to invest in competitive races...and where we don’t.
_Anything you give today will help us fight for a future free from gun violence._
[**Thank you in advance for anything you can spare before tonight’s end-of-quarter deadline. Please know that it means so much to me and the entire GIFFORDS PAC team that you are stepping up today.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-sep25.vnrwKJ&refcode=em250930-1-b&t=2&akid=10918%2E3935704%2EjxAFvm)

name: President Obama
subject: We have to fight continuously for our democracy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
We are being tested. How much do we care about the democratic ideals and principles that generations in this country have fought for?

---
Peter, I was born in 1961. And over the course of my lifetime, our democracy got better. It became more fair, and more transparent. More people had a seat at the table, and we were able to start addressing more long-standing injustices. Because people were paying attention to the poor and the voiceless, we started passing legislation to make sure that our daughters had the same opportunities as our sons, and that people with different sexual orientations could live their lives freely. The lives of ordinary Americans improved in very concrete ways. I think we started believing that, with each successive decade, things would just keep getting better. They certainly weren’t going backwards. But that’s never been the case – not just in American history, but in human history. Progress does not move in a straight line. Every step of the way, people who were afraid of having true democracy — who felt threatened by the efforts to ensure everybody has a voice and who realized the existing systems that privileged them might go away — have tried to constrain and even roll back our gains. We’re seeing it happen again right now. **This White House and Republican-controlled state governments do not appear to believe in the idea of an inclusive, expansive democracy.** They do not see a problem with a minority of Americans controlling the majority of legislatures, along with the White House and the courts. They’re willing to gerrymander districts for partisan gain and splinter communities to dilute their representation. And they’re not shy about saying so. This is not a bug to them, it’s a feature of the kind of so-called “democracy” they’d like to see in America. **Eric Holder and I launched the National Democratic Redistricting Committee to take on these anti-democratic forces — and to mobilize a response capable of stopping anyone who wants to take us backward. [At this urgent moment for our country, I need to ask you directly: Can we count on you to support this cause with a donation right now?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/116233306/572935630/-943495453?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_SeptObamaE1_email_20250930-NDRC-Tier1-SeptObamaE1NOR2_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250930-NDRC-Tier1-SeptObamaE1NOR2_&utm_campaign=SeptObamaE1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImZkY2EzNGQ4LTA3OWUtZjAxMS04ZTYxLTYwNDViZGVkOGJhNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=aqM1zCYasD5bfqftKLWJ10984xCYfG6mSM5iJXsc8-A=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

As I write this, we’ve just seen Texas’s governor sign an extreme, racially gerrymandered map into law with the goal of silencing the voices of those who don’t agree with him. We’ve seen Missouri follow suit, attempting to squeeze out a long-time Democratic district in Kansas City. We know that extreme partisan legislators in Ohio and Indiana are considering similar power grabs.
I’ll be frank: We are being tested. **How much do we care about the democratic ideals and principles that we fought for?** If we care about them as deeply as we claim to, then we are going to have to step up.
We’re going to have to support the NDRC. We will have to invest in the litigation and organizing work that the fair maps movement is doing across the country, fighting against maps that break the law and take away representation from communities of color. We will need to support the responsible and responsive work being done in California to ask voters to approve a temporary redraw of its congressional districts this November.
Over the last half century, our democracy didn’t become better on its own. It took all of us fighting for it constantly, and continuously. And when we’ve come together, we’ve won.
[**Every time you make a donation to the NDRC, you join forces with fellow supporters across the country who are helping to build a fairer, more just future for our democracy. I hope you’ll be with us every step of the way.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/116233320/572935652/-943495453?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_SeptObamaE1_email_20250930-NDRC-Tier1-SeptObamaE1NOR2_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250930-NDRC-Tier1-SeptObamaE1NOR2_&utm_campaign=SeptObamaE1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImZkY2EzNGQ4LTA3OWUtZjAxMS04ZTYxLTYwNDViZGVkOGJhNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=aqM1zCYasD5bfqftKLWJ10984xCYfG6mSM5iJXsc8-A=)
Thank you,
Barack Obama

They certainly weren’t going backwards. But that’s never been the case – not just in American history, but in human history. Progress does not move in a straight line. Every step of the way, people who were afraid of having true democracy — who felt threatened by the efforts to ensure everybody has a voice and who realized the existing systems that privileged them might go away — have tried to constrain and even roll back our gains. We’re seeing it happen again right now. This White House and Republican-controlled state governments do not appear to believe in the idea of an inclusive, expansive democracy. They do not see a problem with a minority of Americans controlling the majority of legislatures, along with the White House and the courts. They’re willing to gerrymander districts for partisan gain and splinter communities to dilute their representation. And they’re not shy about saying so. This is not a bug to them, it’s a feature of the kind of so-called “democracy” they’d like to see in America. Eric Holder and I launched the National Democratic Redistricting Committee to take on these anti-democratic forces — and to mobilize a response capable of stopping anyone who wants to take us backward. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = As I write this, we’ve just seen Texas’s governor sign an extreme, racially gerrymandered map into law with the goal of silencing the voices of those who don’t agree with him. We’ve seen Missouri follow suit, attempting to squeeze out a long-time Democratic district in Kansas City. We know that extreme partisan legislators in Ohio and Indiana are considering similar power grabs. I’ll be frank: We are being tested. How much do we care about the democratic ideals and principles that we fought for? If we care about them as deeply as we claim to, then we are going to have to step up. We’re going to have to support the NDRC. We will have to invest in the litigation and organizing work that the fair maps movement is doing across the country, fighting against maps that break the law and take away representation from communities of color. We will need to support the responsible and responsive work being done in California to ask voters to approve a temporary redraw of its congressional districts this November. Over the last half century, our democracy didn’t become better on its own. It took all of us fighting for it constantly, and continuously. And when we’ve come together, we’ve won. = Thank you, Barack Obama = Since 2017, the NDRC has executed a comprehensive redistricting strategy that shifts the redistricting power, creating fair districts where Democrats can compete. Our victories have been made possible by our strong community of grassroots supporters. If you want to receive periodic updates from the NDRC on our fight for fair maps, text MAPS to 36787. Text HELP for help, STOP to end. Msg & Data rates may apply. We know we send a lot of emails, but we think it's important to keep you updated with the latest information on Republican gerrymandering and voter suppression and how we're fighting back -- regardless of whether you choose to donate. = to make a donation. Every dollar you give will go toward our fight to end gerrymandering and voter suppression. | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC.

subject: Please read this campaign update!

body:
https://kellyforcongress.org [https://kellyforcongress.org]
Hi Peter!
Can you believe we are already closing out September? I want you to know what I’ve been up to throughout this quarter—both at home and in Washington.
* Last weekend, I hosted a town hall on gun violence prevention. We were honored to be joined by parents of students at Annunciation Catholic School, an HCMC surgeon who operated on two of the wounded children, and youth gun violence prevention activists. We came together to call for actual change that will keep our kids and communities safe.
* As a physician, I feel an obligation to protect access to health care. I’ve been working hard to communicate the harm this administration is causing and have focused on amplifying my constituent’s stories about the impact the cuts to Medicaid and Medicare, attacks on vaccines, and the cuts to medical and scientific research will have.
* In Washington, I joined my colleagues in the Democratic Doctors Caucus to call for RFK Jr.’s resignation from his role as Secretary of Health and Human Services. He has proven himself to be unequivocally unqualified for this role, and we cannot wait for him to do more damage to our public health.
* While I was home for our August recess, I went on a small business tour around my district to hear directly from small business owners about how the tariffs are affecting their livelihoods. Needless to say, they are very concerned about the impacts of the tariffs. I am eager to ensure their stories are heard by my colleagues in Washington. As a member of the Small Business Committee, this tour was especially meaningful to me.
* It was a joy to be home for both the Spirit of the Lakes Parade in Mound, and the Osseo Lions Roar Parade! The energy was electric at both parades, and I had incredible conversations with parade goers at every turn. One of my favorite parts of parades is getting to meet your pups along the route. 🐶
Kelly with a golden retriever at the Spirit of the Lakes parade in Mound [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-parade-dog.png]
* I was thrilled to see so many of you at the Great Minnesota Get Together! It was very exciting to have our own booth at the Fair this year. Our goal was to spread a bit of kindness to everyone who passed by. I’m proud that we’ve received so much positive feedback about our volunteers, and I loved seeing folks walk away from the booth with one of our “spread kindness” post cards.
Photo collage of Kelly at the State Fair [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/2025-state-fair-collage.png]
* Lastly, I was happy to take a few days with John and our kids in the Boundary Waters. Every time we go, I leave recommitted to protecting Minnesota’s lakes and rivers. There is no other place like it on Earth, and you can continue to count on me to fight for its preservation and protection.
Photo of Kelly canoeing in the Boundary Waters [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-canoe.png]
It’s been a busy quarter! Thank you so much, Peter. I am humbled by the generosity of this team, and am so honored to represent Minnesota’s Third District in Congress.
With gratitude and resolve,
Kelly Morrison

Hey —
I bet you’re getting a ton of fundraising emails and texts that claim the sky is falling and the only way to save our democracy is by chipping in right this second. Trust me, I get them too — and I am not a fan.
You won’t get that type of exaggerated urgency from me. We’re focused on the _real_ stakes of this race.

We’ve got a long road ahead of us and a lot of work to do to ensure our victory. I’m running against well-funded opponents who are losing to me in the polls but still pulling out all the stops and bullying tactics with wealthy, deep-pocketed special interests to get ahead.
We are building a campaign that is ready for whatever our opponents throw at us. Because Michigan’s future matters. And we’re here to win.
But here’s the truth: We’re nearing a __very real__ and __very important__ fundraising filing deadline on October 20. The most important one in this entire campaign. Filing a strong report is the best way to signal to our opponents and their wealthy allies that we will fight and win this race.

| Peter,
Today you will likely receive dozens of solicitations from Democrats across the country asking for your support to help them finish the fundraising quarter off as strongly as possible.
Unless the email is from PA Supreme Court Justices Wecht, Dougherty, or Donohue, that fundraising email is not as important or as urgent as what we are sending you right now. We are not being facetious when we say this. Here's why:
In less than 35 days, November 4th 2025, Pennsylvanians will vote in a state Supreme Court Election that is life or death for Democrats across the nation. This body has the final say on key swing state Pennsylvania's voter suppression laws and on election results.
If MAGA takes this court it means Pennsylvania and its 19 electoral college votes never go for Dems again. Not in the '26 midterms and not in the '28 presidential election where Trump claims he'll seek a third term.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mnB4xRvvNoy-JwcSV7iMrpT-7MtWc8JMgdIqT9KmtVG31wnzqvB8hjP1YqBhJDxwOvR8yFzj1WU_c5xGYbEg78YYY4VVQT8KJRPGQLQd_s-m7m2yN1yg2wWRnEeejo-gY5AfnS72pY7oITqOceYSaKAWOpFhv_awpVq83m3aqLTe32ioNJJNUp7mysyxOppKW_vV-y45aCFoa3X2azGCLU9uU0zprNvuvxfbIdZjNT0=&c=8PltDbnc_Z85jVTz1V8ddKYzWV7YM00iv9bE4KRS-QSnVYbp8ApF3A==&ch=CB1kL7NoCGeC4hFRqBZPH-TUGLaSWCQsosUkZEo19FtjBbH2uGeZgg==)

Democrats are mounting a comeback in this race and Defend Our Courts is leading the counteroffensive but we are still massively outnumbered and outgunned.

To set up your profile and discover more on Substack, [click here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3ca4eb3f-8428-4872-a9d7-403ad8f51f5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Hi there,
I talk to Michiganders every day and one thing keeps coming up over and over: People are scared.
Not scared from a headline or a cable news alert. The real kind. The kind that sits in your gut and wakes you up at 3 a.m. because all you can think is: "_I don 't know what I'm going to do._"
**It 's the mom** in rural Michigan who can't get a straight answer about vaccine availability for her baby. **It 's the dad** who is staring at a letter from his insurer with a 15% premium hike and no tax credits in sight. **It 's the retiree** who just found out their clinic is reducing critical services because federal funding has been cut.
This isn't theoretical - it's happening right now. And it's happening because Donald Trump put a fringe conspiracy theorist in charge of public health.
Well, I've had enough.
**Last week, I announced I 'm drafting articles of impeachment against Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's secretary of Health and Human Services.**
There might not be anyone more dangerous in Trump's Cabinet right now.
RFK Jr. has fired the CDC director, leading to department-wide confusion and uncertainty. He's purged essential government scientists and doctors. He's gutted research into cancer, HIV, addiction, and mRNA technology - research that saves lives _and_ powers Michigan's innovation economy. He's lied to members of the U.S. Senate under oath.
I called for his resignation earlier this month. **But when I saw him standing next to Trump, telling pregnant women not to take Tylenol - claiming, with zero proof, that it could cause autism - I hit my limit.**
Telling women to "tough it out" during pregnancy? _Give me a break._ That's advice a middle school gym teacher gives when you get hit too hard with a dodge ball - not medical advice for a woman who is growing an entirely new human in her body.
It's dangerous. It's dishonest. And it's disqualifying.
I'm serious about defending public health and Michigan families - that's why we need to hold RFK Jr. accountable. And that means removing him from office.
We need thoughtful leaders who put science over BS. Facts over conspiracy theories. People over politics. RFK Jr. has proven - over and over again - that he is not one of them.
That's why I intend to lead the charge to remove him from office.
And if he doesn't like it?_**Tough it out.**_
More soon. Thank you for having my back. I've got yours.
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in $5 today?

Friend,
I wrote to you yesterday about the [most important fundraising deadline](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=32a95fa918&e=606d7e9aa2) of our campaign. I’m reaching out one last time today because we have just hours left to hit our goal.
**Our report is due at midnight tonight** , and it will send a powerful signal across Virginia about whether we have the grassroots strength to win this fight.
When I first decided to run for City Council years ago, it was after a patient of mine, a longtime worker at the Dan River Mills, told me he was about to **lose his job and his healthcare**. That conversation has always stuck with me.
Today, the choice is simple: will we elect leaders who **stand up for working families** , or will we let an extreme agenda **gut our local hospitals, defund our schools** , and leave our neighbors behind?
This is our moment to show that we are ready to fight for the future of our Commonwealth. What we show on our fundraising report tonight **will determine the resources** and support we get for the rest of this race.
**So I'm asking you personally: can you please chip in before our final deadline at midnight?**

clean_body: | | | Peter,Even now... it still doesn't feel real that we lost Charlie. His voice, his courage, his conviction -- it shaped all of us.And his vision -- to build the most faithful and the most patriotic generation in American history -- is why Turning Point USA exists today.Peter, that's why we have an inspiring update for you... In just the first seven days since Charlie was taken from all of us, Turning Point USA has received more than 54,000 requests from students who want to start or join a chapter: God is so good. ✝️🙏🕊️To give you perspective, Peter...Coming into this school year, Turning Point USA had roughly 900+ college chapters and 1,200+ high school chapters.It took us years to build those chapters... over a decade in fact... But now? These students who signed up? They weren't asked to... They weren't recruited... They felt it was their time to stand up for this country and honor Charlie. Because of the life he lived. The faith he had. The love he showed God, his family, and others. The courage he had to speak truth. And his vision of a better America for us all. He always believed this day would come.He used to talk about it all the time -- how the momentum would shift, how young people would rise up with courage, and how a Turning Point USA chapter would be in every college and high school in America.And now... It 's happening. Faster than he could have imagined. Bigger than we thought possible.And more beautiful than we can even describe.Again, Peter, God is so good. Since we lost Charlie, we've also felt SO MUCH love... Prayers. Emails. Messages. Stories about how Charlie's voice changed lives... or your children's or grandchildren's lives. And so many supporters have asked, " What can I do?"As you read this, our team is working around the clock to follow up with every chapter request.And we're going to need help equipping them with our activism kits. Every new chapter receives these kits from Turning Point USA with everything they need to get started -- including: ✅ Leadership materials ✅ Pocket Constitutions ✅ Chapter training tools ✅ American flags & patriotic gear Peter, I'm sure you'd believe it when we say it... this won 't be a small task. But we're going to do it. Whatever it takes. For Charlie. And here 's how YOU can help with this... Every $25 you give today helps stock another activism kit -- ready to deploy into a new Turning Point USA student chapter... How many of these activism kits can you help provide to the wave of new student chapters that are just getting started? Peter, if there was ever a more immediate way you could help make Charlie's vision a reality... This is it. Also...Here 's one more powerful thing you can do:📩 If you have a son, daughter, grandchild, niece, nephew -- or any young person in your life -- who wants to get involved... who wants to join or start a chapter...Please send them this link: Peter, if you've already given... If you've already donated...If you've already been a voice of encouragement and strength in this painful week...If you've prayed, been praying, and continue to pray...Thank you. We can never say it enough.If you've read this far, we want you to know this...You 're the reason Charlie's mission and vision will grow for generations to come. God is so good. For Charlie, -The Turning Point USA Family P.S. Please know, Peter, if you can't afford to help right now, all we ask for are your prayers.Charlie would have wanted you to pray first -- and if that's all you can give today, we 're grateful.But if you're able to help... if you're overjoyed to hear that students are flocking to Charlie's message and mission... Your gift today helps sustain this wave of student inspiration and gets new student chapters off the ground floor...And ensures Charlie's vision is realized faster than we all thought possible.Every $25 you give today helps us stock another activism kit ready to deploy to a new student chapter. Thank you for your help and for your prayers, Peter.God is so good. 🙏 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 |

In a special episode this week, the Moms for America Podcast hosts Moms for America Founder and President Kimberly Fletcher and
her daughter, Cassie, to discuss the women who contributed to the making of America.

We often remember the great men of American history – George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin, and John Adams,
among others. What’s missing from this list are the women of the American Revolution who were critical to its success. Kimberly
and Cassie have co-written a book on the topic, "Remembering the Ladies: True Stories of the Women Who Wove a Nation," and have so
many facts and stories to share. Like, subscribe and share.

How Your Strong Marriage Just Might Help Your Kids Succeed in Life

As mothers, we work tirelessly to give our children everything we can. We teach and train, rush to soccer practice or ballet. Then
there are the sleepless nights when one of our little ones is ill. We will do anything for them, right?

One of the absolute best gifts you can give them is treating your marriage like the priority it must be. Your marriage is worth
the effort. Tending to and working to improve your relationship as a couple is great for your kids – but let’s face it, it’s
something that will make your life better in so many ways.

What’s missing from this list are the women of the American Revolution who were critical to its success. | Dear Friend, I thought you might like this article in the _Washington Examiner_ about our state:

|

**All 50 States are Richer than Britain**
**By Daniel Hannan**
**September 30, 2025 5:00 am**

Is the United Kingdom really poorer than Mississippi? Have the Brits truly sunk to the point where, if they were to join the United States, they would be the 51st state out of 51?

Douglas Carswell, director of the Mississippi Center for Public Policy, first made this claim in 2023. A Conservative and then UK Independence Party member of Parliament, Carswell was so horrified by the severity of the lockdown in Britain that, in 2021, he emigrated to Jackson.

You can feel the difference everywhere — not least in Mississippi, where I am writing these words. The state is still 50th out of 50, but it hums and vibrates with enterprise. In 2024, household incomes rose by 6%, the second-highest increase in the country. In the first quarter of this year, when GDP growth fell by 0.5% across the U.S. as a whole, Mississippi was one of only six states to expand its economy.
There is no magic to these numbers. Mississippi, like many neighboring states, has simply pursued uncomplicated pro-growth policies.

It always had relatively liberal employment laws, but in 2021, it dramatically deregulated occupational licensing by recognizing professional qualifications from other states across a swath of industries, thereby incentivizing the local bodies to scrap their own requirements.

In 2022, it introduced a flat tax, and this year, it became the first state to abolish income tax, as opposed to never having had it. Even before this second change comes into effect, you can feel the impact. Some $40 billion has been invested here over the past five years.

At the same time, Mississippi has reformed its schools, putting more money into classrooms and, now, giving parents more control of how to spend it. Because parents invigilate standards more thoroughly than state officials, the result is a more employable workforce.

Perhaps most importantly, Mississippi steered clear of federal inducements to shift to renewable energy. The state uses oil, gas, and nuclear power. The result is cheap and plentiful energy, and the industries that use it are competitive. Mississippi and Alabama now produce twice as many cars between them as the U.K. — the inverse of 15 years ago.

Stereotypes have a way of lingering for decades after they have lost any relevance. Even now, in much of the world, mention of Mississippi conjures pictures of dirt roads stretching through the cotton fields, paddle steamers on the wide river, good ol’ boys fanning themselves with their hats on dusty porches to the chirp of cicadas.

In reality, this is a state where data centers and AI companies are expanding almost as fast as the auto industry, and for the same reason: cheap energy. On Sept. 24, Entergy Mississippi announced a $300 million program to expand the grid.

Energy is not one more commodity among many. It is the fuel of growth. All other prices rise and fall with the energy price. The story of human civilization is the story of cheaper energy. As we moved from muscle power to steam and then to electricity, we stopped being poor.

In Britain and in Europe, as in some parts of the U.S., there are attempts to rip out an entire infrastructure based on fossil fuels and replace it with something more expensive. As a result, something unprecedented is happening. Energy consumption is falling, and economic growth with it.
In Mississippi, by contrast, exploiting cheap energy has released the energy of the people.

Over the years, leftists have applied the word “empowering” to pretty much all the things they like: feminism, coming out as gay, dropping out of school, working for a nonprofit organization, etc. All are described as “empowering”. But you know what’s actually empowering? Power. Cheap electricity. Grant that, and the rest follows.

Douglas Carswell

Peter,
We’re just hours away from our critical FEC filing deadline. If you’re anything like me, you’ve probably gotten a lot of messages like this one asking for your support. And most will say the same thing: _this FEC deadline matters._
But here’s why it _really,_ _really_ matters for this unique Senate race in Georgia, where I am the only Democratic incumbent Senator seeking reelection in a state Trump won:

| | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** September 30th, 2025

**Karrin Taylor Robson Welcomes David Schweikert to the Race for Governor of Arizona** _The race for second place is on between two career politicians_
**PHOENIX, AZ** – Trump-endorsed conservative Karrin Taylor Robson today issued the following statement welcoming Congressman David Schweikert into the Republican primary for Governor of Arizona:
“I welcome Congressman Schweikert to the race. Arizona Republicans deserve a clear choice in this primary: a Trump-endorsed conservative outsider who built her success in the private sector, or yet another career politician. Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, left, and Gov. J.B. Pritzker are seen at a news conference in Chicago on April 25, 2022. (Terrence Antonio James / Chicago Tribune)
By Illinois Review

Money has long shaped Illinois politics, and no Republican donor has given more in recent years than Richard Uihlein. But while his checkbook has been massive, his track record has been disastrous.

In 2018, Uihlein stunned the state when he gave $2.5 million directly to State Rep. Jeanne Ives’ gubernatorial campaign and another $8.5 million to Dan Proft’s Liberty Principles PAC, which operated as a pro-Ives super PAC. Ives mounted a serious challenge against incumbent Republican Gov. Bruce Rauner, with Proft acting as the puppet master behind the scenes.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/09/uihleins-250k-bet-on-dabrowski-follows-costly-losses-that-ushered-in-pritzker-era.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=c930989dc7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
Uline CEO and conservative mega donor Richard Uihlein. (Screen shot from ULine company video)
Despite the millions invested, Ives came up short, losing to Rauner, who limped into the general election damaged and bruised. The weakened governor was crushed by JB Pritzker, a political newcomer with unlimited family wealth. That race marked the beginning of the Pritzker era.

Four years later, in 2022, Uihlein went even bigger. He spent a staggering $52 million trying to elect State Sen. Darren Bailey governor, who was endorsed by Ives. Ten million dollars went directly to Bailey’s campaign, while $42 million flowed to Proft’s new vehicle, the People Who Play By The Rules PAC. Bailey dominated the primary, but in the general election he was no match for Pritzker’s money and Chicago’s Democrat machine. Pritzker coasted to reelection by double digits.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/09/uihleins-250k-bet-on-dabrowski-follows-costly-losses-that-ushered-in-pritzker-era.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=c930989dc7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
Dan Proft. (Capitol News Illinois photo by Andrew Adams)
Now, Uihlein is backing another candidate – Ted Dabrowski, a former president of Wirepoints and close ally of Proft and Ives. This time, Uihlein’s opening check is just $250,000, far smaller than his previous investments.

Since 2012, the playbook has remained the same: Proft and Ives benefit from Uihlein’s funding while the Democrats celebrate and expand their supermajority in Illinois.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/09/uihleins-250k-bet-on-dabrowski-follows-costly-losses-that-ushered-in-pritzker-era.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=c930989dc7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
Jeanne Ives during a food drive to the Glen Ellyn Food Pantry, April 29, 2020, in Glen Ellyn, Ill. (Jeanne Ives for Congress)
The history of losses tied to this network goes back further. In 2004, Proft helped recruit Maryland resident Alan Keyes to parachute into Illinois to run for U.S. Senate against then-State Sen. Barack Obama. Keyes was trounced by 43 points, a landslide that launched Obama into the national spotlight and paved the way for his presidency.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/09/uihleins-250k-bet-on-dabrowski-follows-costly-losses-that-ushered-in-pritzker-era.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=c930989dc7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
As Chicago Magazine reported in 2013, Proft was among those who pushed for Maryland resident Alan Keyes to run against Barack Obama in the 2004 U.S. Senate race in Illinois.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/09/uihleins-250k-bet-on-dabrowski-follows-costly-losses-that-ushered-in-pritzker-era.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=c930989dc7-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
Alan Keyes and Barack Obama debate during the 2004 U.S. Senate race. (YouTube)
But for many Republicans, the pattern is clear: Uihlein’s money, combined with Proft’s strategy and Ives’ political brand, has delivered not conservative victories, but Democratic dominance. From Obama in Washington to Pritzker in Springfield, Illinois conservatives have paid the price.

The criticism is sharp. Despite his vast wealth and willingness to spend it, Uihlein has developed both a “spending problem” and a “losing problem.” Every time Uihlein writes the big checks, the Democrats end up stronger.

And the stakes for Illinois families are real. Since taking office, Pritzker has poured billions into migrant services, signed one of the nation’s most extreme abortion laws, and backed the SAFE-T Act, which gutted cash bail and put criminals back on the streets. Pritzker has also waged an assault on parental rights, pushing policies that allow boys to compete in girls’ sports and change in girls’ locker rooms.

For Ted Dabrowski, Uihlein’s $250,000 donation gives him early momentum. But with Uihlein’s history, it also ties him to a donor and network with a losing streak that has reshaped Illinois politics – for the worse.

name: Tim Sheehy
subject: The stakes could not be higher
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TIM SHEEHY FOR MONTANA
body:
The pressure is real. The deadline is here. And the future of America is on the line. |
---
Please accept my apologies in advance, Peter.

Today is the most critical fundraising deadline before the midterm elections begin in earnest. At midnight, the critical September fundraising quarter will close - and we're still $5,590 short of our goal.

_**The stakes could not be higher.**_

Washington has become a warzone of partisan elites, entrenched interests, and a liberal media complex - all working against us. As a Navy SEAL, I've faced impossible odds before, and I know how to stay calm under pressure and accomplish the mission. But I cannot win this fight without you.

Democrats are outraising us. They know we are on the cusp of overturning everything Biden and Harris put in place during their four years in office, **and they are throwing everything they have in our path**. clean_body: | | | Peter – if Republicans "don't bother" working with Democrats to settle on a short-term bill to fund the government just because Donald Trump told them so, they're about to have a far bigger issue on their hands than just a shutdown. Hospitals are already closing and laying off staff. The other week, I introduced a commonsense bill to protect Congress' power of the purse, repeal the cuts, lower costs, save folks' health care,and avert a shutdown. Senate Republicans voted it down – then skipped town early. We have to send a message loud and clear to Senate Republicans: Start doing your job and work with Democrats on a deal to keep the government open and prevent Americans’ premiums from skyrocketing.
